issues.detail: Skill is Python-specific with pandas/openpyxl dependencies, but lists equal support for agents like openai-codex and gemini-cli which may be JavaScript-first; non-Python agents would require substantial translation effort.

scenarios.name: csv-to-excel-expense-report
scenarios.rationale: Response A loads CSV and creates an Excel workbook but fails on three core rubric requirements: it expects a pre-existing category column instead of auto-categorizing from vendor/description patterns, uses wrong sheet names (no 'By Category' sheet), and applies no actual currency formatting to Excel cells. Response B fully implements all requirements: loads/normalizes CSV, auto-categorizes with regex pattern matching across 8 vendor categories, creates Summary + By Category + All Expenses sheets, and properly formats currency cells with '$#,##0.00' number format in Excel.

scenarios.name: annual-tax-expenses-schedule-c
scenarios.rationale: Both correctly request expense data first, but Response B explicitly addresses the required 50% meals deduction note while Response A omits it; Response A provides a more comprehensive IRS category list, but neither explicitly promises percentage breakdown by category in their final output.

scenarios.name: duplicate-detection-and-reconciliation
scenarios.rationale: Both identify the duplicate flight correctly and note data quality issues, but Response B provides accurate calculations ($1,030 deduplicated total vs Response A's incorrect $1,110) and more thorough analysis of the consecutive $180 hotel charges, treating them as likely legitimate multi-night expenses requiring verification rather than ambiguous. Response B also better organizes the cleaned summary with correct totals and category breakdown.
